common_name: Asheville Sunrise Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil; expect a rebloom flush later in the season.

directions: Robert P. Selman registered Asheville Sunrise in 2022 from a complex Lip Smack x Last Fool Standing cross, and it earned the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention, the Society's first official recognition, which requires at least fifteen judges' votes from four or more AHS regions. The dormant tetraploid produces golden yellow, 5.5-inch midseason blooms with a bold red eye and matching picotee edge over a yellow-to-green throat, carried on 31-inch scapes with 18 buds across three branches. Grow divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect a reliable rebloom flush later in the season.

common_name: Nefarious Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Scott Elliott registered the double-form Nefarious in 2017, and the fragrant diploid went on to earn the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. Its crispate, unusual-form petals open as a clean yellow self on 34-inch scapes carrying 32 buds across five branches, blooming early midseason with reliable rebloom. Divide dormant clumps every few years in spring to maintain bud count and keep the ruffled double form expressing well.

common_name: Sea of Glass Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Minnesota hybridizer Karol Emmerich registered the fragrant tetraploid Sea of Glass in 2019, and it received the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention after votes from AHS Garden Judges across multiple regions. Blooms open cranberry grape with an icy gray-lavender eye, a matching icy lavender-and-ivory edge, and a yellow-to-green throat, on 26-inch rebloom scapes carrying 22 buds across four branches. Grow dormant divisions in full sun; Emmerich's Minnesota breeding program is known for producing exceptionally winter-hardy cultivars.

common_name: Bob on My Mind Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Dominique Elliott registered the diploid Bob on My Mind in 2019, and it earned the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. The semi-evergreen rebloomer bears bicolor flowers with dark pink petals edged in a lighter pink above a small green throat, with melon-cream colored sepals, on 27-inch scapes carrying 29 buds across five branches. Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

common_name: Lemonade with Friends Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil; divide crowded clumps every three to four years.

directions: Janice Kennedy registered the unusual-form crispate cultivar Lemonade with Friends in 2019, and it received the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. The dormant diploid produces a lemonade-yellow self with light ruffling and veining on 36-inch midseason scapes carrying 14 buds across four branches. Grow divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, dividing crowded clumps every three to four years.

common_name: The Mayor of Browns Ferry Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Heidi Douglas registered The Mayor of Browns Ferry in 2021, and the cascade-form diploid earned the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. Its reverse-bicolor blooms show yellow petals speckled orange along the edges and midribs above orange sepals with a small green heart, opening on 32-inch rebloom scapes with 18 buds across three branches. Grow dormant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil.

common_name: Jean Clement Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil; allow extra room at the back of a border for its height.

directions: Bret Clement registered the tall cascade-form Jean Clement in 2014, and it earned the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. The dormant diploid bears magenta-rose flowers with a lighter veined watermark over a vivid green throat, held on 49-inch scapes carrying 25 buds across six branches, among the tallest-scaping cultivars to receive the award that year. Give it full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, and allow extra room at the back of a border for its height.

common_name: Double Magnolia Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Hybridizer registered under the name Williams-S. introduced the heavily double Double Magnolia in 2014, and it received the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. The dormant diploid opens cream with a dark purple eye that bleeds outward onto the petals and sepals, on 24-inch scapes carrying 12 buds across two branches. Plant divisions in spring in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil.

common_name: Uncle Henry of Oz Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Katisue Herrington registered the fully double, fragrant Uncle Henry of Oz in 2007, and it received the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention nearly two decades after its introduction. The semi-evergreen tetraploid reblooms with red-orange blend flowers edged lighter, on 30-inch scapes carrying 35 buds across five branches. Grow divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil.

common_name: Italian Summer Daylily (2025 AHS Honorable Mention Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, fertile well-drained soil.

directions: Tim Bell registered the fragrant tetraploid Italian Summer in 2018, and it earned the American Hemerocallis Society's 2025 Honorable Mention. The evergreen rebloomer bears golden copper flowers with a patterned eye in shades of purple and violet over a green throat, on 30-inch early-midseason scapes carrying 28 buds across four branches. Grow divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil.
